cues.en: Lift off.
cues.zh: 升空。

cues.en: We have list off.
cues.zh: 我们已离地。

cues.en: When it's my life on the line, what type of a team do I want out there holding it in their palm? And the answer I came to is I think the identical answer you would come to in the identical circumstance.
cues.zh: 当我的生命悬于一线，我想要什么样的团队把它捧在掌心？我得出的答案，我想和你在同样处境下会得出的答案完全一样。

cues.en: When your life is on the line, you're gonna want a team that's the best holding in their palm. And how do teams get to be the best? They get there by practicing fundamentals,
cues.zh: 当你的生命悬于一线，你会想要最优秀的团队把它捧在掌心。那团队怎样才能变得最优秀？靠练习基本功，

cues.en: by doing little things consistently and religiously day in and day out until they become as natural as breathing. You don't even think about them. Now there's lots of fundamentals out there, but there are three that I think have overarching importance to the success and safety of all teams everywhere and those are the three that I want to talk about this morning.
cues.zh: 靠日复一日、虔诚而始终如一地做好那些小事，直到它们变得像呼吸一样自然。你甚至都不用去想它们。基本功有很多，但我认为有三项对各地所有团队的成功与安全具有头等重要性，这就是我今天上午想讲的三项。

cues.en: When I'm involved with any team,
cues.zh: 当我参与任何团队时，

cues.en: but particularly when there are lethal consequences associated with the team environment as there as there are with you in firefighting
cues.zh: 尤其是当团队环境伴随着致命后果时——就像你们在消防

cues.en: and emergency response
cues.zh: 和应急响应中那样，

cues.en: just as it is in the space program. People die
cues.zh: 就像在太空计划中一样。人会死，

cues.en: when they don't understand the dangers of a normalization of deviance and protect themselves against that. And I'm gonna talk about that. I'll define that here for you in just a moment. I want everybody on the team under the... Understanding the essence of responsibility as it applies to the individual as well as it applies to the leadership.
cues.zh: 当他们不理解偏差正常化的危险、不据此保护自己时。我就要讲这个。我稍后会在这里为你们定义它。我希望团队里的每个人都理解责任感的本质，既适用于个人，也适用于领导层。

cues.en: And I want a team that's filled with courageous self leaders.
cues.zh: 我想要一支充满勇气、能自我领导的团队。

cues.en: I think Harold really kind of hit on that in his earlier comments.
cues.zh: 我觉得 Harold 在之前的发言里确实点到了这一点。

cues.en: It's self leadership that determines how safe and successful you can be. It's looking deep inside yourself. It can't... And it every... Has to be everybody practicing self leadership for the team to succeed.
cues.zh: 正是自我领导力决定了你能有多安全、多成功。这需要深入审视自己。这不能……而且这……必须每个人都践行自我领导，团队才能成功。

cues.en: It can't be 99 out of a 100. Every individual, again, particularly in hazardous environments has to be a courageous self leader.
cues.zh: 不能是百分之一百里的九十九个。每一个人，再强调一次，尤其是在危险环境中，都必须是勇敢的自我领导者。

cues.en: So I'll just talk about that as part of this teamwork program. Now I'm gonna use some experiences I had both as an Air Force flyer and as a NASA astronaut to develop some points on these fundamentals.
cues.zh: 所以我会把这作为团队协作项目的一部分来讲。接下来我会用自己在空军当飞行员和在 NASA 当宇航员的经历，来展开这些基本原则的一些要点。

cues.en: And sadly, NASA provides me with two great tragedies to draw from to make some points. Those tragedies being the Challenger disaster and the Columbia disaster.
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，NASA 给了我两场重大悲剧可以用来举例说明。这两场悲剧就是挑战者号灾难和哥伦比亚号灾难。

cues.en: Now Columbia occurred four years ago. I think everybody's kind of familiar with that disaster. During launch, some foam came off the gas tank, damaged the heat shield. Two weeks later, Columbia burned up on reentry, killing seven astronauts.
cues.zh: 哥伦比亚号发生在四年前。我想大家多少都熟悉那场灾难。发射时，一些泡沫从外储箱上脱落，损伤了隔热层。两周后，哥伦比亚号在再入时烧毁，七名宇航员罹难。

cues.en: People are probably familiar with that that disaster. Whereas Challenger goes back twenty one years ago, past January,
cues.zh: 大家可能对那场灾难比较熟悉。而挑战者号要追溯到二十一年前的那个一月，

cues.en: long time in the past. So I imagine most of you are probably foggy in your memories what caused the Challenger to be lost. And because I will be referencing that program
cues.zh: 已经很久远了。所以我猜你们大多数人可能对挑战者号失事的原因记忆模糊了。因为我在这个项目里会提到

cues.en: in the... Referencing that disaster in this program, I wanna take a moment to briefly review for you mechanically what caused the loss of the space shuttle Challenger.
cues.zh: 在这个……在这个项目里会提到那场灾难，我想花点时间简要回顾一下，从机械层面讲，是什么导致了挑战者号航天飞机的失事。

cues.en: Challenger was a failure of the right hand solid rocket booster.
cues.zh: Challenger 号的失事，是右侧固体火箭助推器故障导致的。

cues.en: These things are so big. They're a 150 feet long, 12 feet in diameter, and each of them weighs 1,300,000
cues.zh: 这些助推器非常巨大。它们长 150 英尺、直径 12 英尺，每个重 1,300,000

cues.en: pounds. They're too big to be made in one piece at the factory in Utah and shipped in one piece down to Florida where they're launched. So they build them in four propellant filled pieces that are shipped separately by flatbed railcar from the Thycol plant in Utah down to the Vertical Assembly Building at Cape Kennedy. There, these segments are stacked on top of each other to form twin towers of boosters.
cues.zh: 磅。它们太大，无法在犹他州的工厂里一体制造，再整体运到佛罗里达的发射场。所以它们被做成四段装满推进剂的部件，由平板轨道车从犹他州的 Thycol 工厂分别运到肯尼迪角的垂直装配大楼。在那里，这些段被逐段堆叠起来，组成两座助推器塔。

cues.en: The gas tank is hung between the boosters.
cues.zh: 外贮箱悬挂在助推器之间。

cues.en: The wing vehicles attached to the gas tank and then all of this is taken out to the launch pad on this 9,000,000 pound mobile launch platform.
cues.zh: 带翼飞行器固定在外贮箱上，然后整套系统被放到这个重 9,000,000 磅的移动发射平台上，运往发射台。

cues.en: Now when these boosters ignite, they burn at 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit and at a pressure of about a thousand psi.
cues.zh: 当这些助推器点火时，它们以华氏 5,000 度、约 1000 psi 的压力燃烧。

cues.en: Steel boils at 5,000 degrees. So you have to ensure in your design that the steel of the booster is never touched by the fire that it contains.
cues.zh: 钢在 5,000 度就会沸腾。所以设计中必须确保助推器的钢体永远不会接触到内部的火焰。

cues.en: So there's insulating material to run the inside length of these segments.
cues.zh: 因此有隔热材料沿这些段的内壁全长铺设。

cues.en: The obvious weak point in this design is where you've bolted these segments together because there you have a potential leak path for the gas to pass to the outside, melt the steel, and cause a catastrophe.
cues.zh: 这个设计明显的薄弱点，就是各段被螺栓连接在一起的地方，因为那里存在潜在泄漏通道，气体可能窜到外部、熔化钢体并引发灾难。

cues.en: Now I'm not gonna go into the engineering specifics
cues.zh: 我不打算深入讲工程细节

cues.en: of the joint design that was intended to prevent such gas leakage other than to say it was based on a redundant flexible o ring scheme. Two flexible o rings. Here's a piece of one of them right here. 12 foot in diameter at each perim... At each perimeter of those segment of those segment joints. Two of them in each joint were supposed to form a redundant steel to steel pressure seal to prevent the fire from leaking out. On Challenger, both o rings fail on the bottom segment of the right side solid rocket booster. Here's Challenger coming off the launch pad. In that yellow area, you'll see a black smoke being ejected. That's the vaporized o rings being shoved out that bottom joint. You now have 5,000 degrees eating into that outer wall. As the rocket flies higher, the gas is vaporizing a bigger and bigger hole in the side of the booster rocket. Seventy three seconds into flight, the rocket comes apart killing the seven astronauts.
cues.zh: 也就是那个原本用于防止气体泄漏的接头设计，我只想说，它基于冗余柔性 O 型圈方案。两个柔性 O 型圈。这里有一块其中一个 O 型圈的片段。直径 12 英尺，环绕每个段接头的圆周。每个接头里的两个 O 型圈本应形成冗余的钢对钢压力密封，防止火焰外泄。在 Challenger 号上，右侧固体火箭助推器底部段的两个 O 型圈都失效了。这是 Challenger 号离开发射台时的画面。在那个黄色区域，你会看到喷出的黑烟。那就是汽化的 O 型圈被从底部接头挤出来。现在 5,000 度高温正在烧蚀外壁。随着火箭飞得更高，气体在助推器侧面烧出的洞越来越大。飞行 73 秒后，火箭解体，7 名宇航员丧生。

cues.en: Now what you're seeing here appears to be an explosion but was not. This was a catastrophic structural breakup.
cues.zh: 你在这里看到的看起来像爆炸，但其实不是。这是一次灾难性的结构解体。

cues.en: The fire weakened the attachment to the bottom of the goo... Bottom of the of the gas tank.
cues.zh: 火焰削弱了它与底部黏合处……燃料箱底部的连接。

cues.en: That bottom just basically fell off. The top of the booster rotated into the top of the gas tank rupturing at that. And under the aerodynamic and geoloads of the moment, the vehicle just the vehicle just shredded itself. Nothing detonated, nothing blew up. That will become important to remember downstream
cues.zh: 那个底部基本上就脱落了。助推器顶部旋转撞入燃料箱顶部，并在那里造成破裂。在当时的空气动力载荷和 G 载荷下，飞行器就……飞行器就这么被撕碎了。没有任何东西起爆，没有任何东西爆炸。这一点在后续会变得很重要，要记住

cues.en: when we talk about crew survivability associated with this tragedy.
cues.zh: 当我们谈论这场悲剧中与乘员生存能力有关的问题时。

cues.en: Now you're going to need that background to understand some of my downstream comments. And certainly you're going to need it to understand my comments about normalization of deviance.
cues.zh: 现在你们需要这个背景，才能理解我后面的一些评论。当然，你们也需要它来理解我关于偏差正常化的评论。

cues.en: What is this? Well, it's that natural human tendency,
cues.zh: 这是什么？嗯，就是那种人类天生的倾向，

cues.en: particularly in pressure circumstances
cues.zh: 尤其是在压力环境下

cues.en: to want to take shortcuts,
cues.zh: 想要走捷径，

cues.en: to accept a lower standard of performance.
cues.zh: 接受更低的表现标准。

cues.en: Maybe it's a lower standard of personal performance,
cues.zh: 也许是更低的个人表现标准，

cues.en: a lower standard performance for some team you lead, lower standard performance for some machine
cues.zh: 对你领导的某个团队采用更低的表现标准，对某台机器采用更低的表现标准

cues.en: firefighting
cues.zh: 消防

cues.en: equipment that you oversee.
cues.zh: 你所监管的设备。

cues.en: But it's very human to find yourself in pressure circumstances and God knows you folks find it on every call.
cues.zh: 但人在压力环境下会这样，这非常人性；天知道你们每次出警都会遇到。

cues.en: Very human to find yourself in a pressure circumstance and rationalize,
cues.zh: 人在压力环境下会给自己找理由，这非常人性，

cues.en: I can't execute to meet these standards I've been trained to meet. I'm going have to take a shortcut.
cues.zh: 我无法执行到满足我受训要达到的这些标准。我不得不走捷径。

cues.en: Maybe the shortcut is what Harold was talking about, not doing a proper risk assessment.
cues.zh: 也许捷径就是Harold所说的，没做正经的风险评估。

cues.en: Maybe it's not having the right communication in place.
cues.zh: 也许是没做好正确的沟通。

cues.en: Maybe it's not wearing the right protective equipment, whatever.
cues.zh: 也许是没穿戴正确的防护装备，等等。

cues.en: But it's very human to in pressure to rationalize I can't do this job and meet the standards.
cues.zh: 但人在压力下很自然会合理化：我干不了这活还达标。

cues.en: I'm going to have to take a shortcut.
cues.zh: 我只能走捷径。

cues.en: And so you take that shortcut and guess what the consequences are.
cues.zh: 于是你走了捷径，猜猜后果是什么。

cues.en: There are no bad consequences. You aren't injured. Nobody's injured.
cues.zh: 没有任何坏后果。你没受伤，也没人受伤。

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 应急

cues.en: response, the emergency response proceeds successfully.
cues.zh: 响应，应急响应顺利推进。

cues.en: There are no bad consequences to your actions in taking that shortcut.
cues.zh: 你走捷径的行为没有任何坏后果。

cues.en: What's that gonna do? It's gonna loop it back loop it back into your brain and reinforce the rightness of that earlier decision to take the shortcut in the first place.
cues.zh: 这会怎样？它会回路，回传到你的大脑，强化你最初决定走捷径的正确性。

cues.en: So what's liable to happen the very next time you find yourself in these same pressure circumstances?
cues.zh: 那么下次你再处于同样的压力环境时，很可能发生什么？

cues.en: And I guarantee there's going to be a next time, particularly particularly in your businesses.
cues.zh: 我保证一定会有下一次，尤其在你们的行业里。

cues.en: Because there were no bad consequences the last time you took the shortcut, you're going to be mightily tempted to do it again. You do it enough times and what happens?
cues.zh: 因为上次走捷径没有坏后果，你会极想再来一次。做得够多会怎样？

cues.en: The shortcut becomes the norm. Here are the standards that you're expected to be meeting. Here's where you are in execution.
cues.zh: 捷径成了常态。这些是你应该达到的标准。这是你实际执行的情况。

cues.en: This deviance is invisible to you. You don't even think about it.
cues.zh: 这种偏差对你不可见。你甚至想都不会想。

cues.en: It has become normalized into your actions and to your team actions. And what happens with normalization of deviance, it leads to predictable surprises.
cues.zh: 这种做法已经融入了你和团队的行动之中。而偏差正常化会带来什么后果？它会导致可预见的意外。

cues.en: And if you ever want... And and I'll tell you, in hazardous environments,
cues.zh: 如果你想要一个例子……我告诉你，在危险环境中，

cues.en: predictable surprises on the job can be injurious and they can be deadly.
cues.zh: 工作中那些可预见的意外可能造成伤害，甚至致命。

cues.en: If you ever want an object lesson in the... In what a... What normalization of deviance can do, a predictable surprise,
cues.zh: 如果你想通过一个实例了解……了解偏差正常化会造成什么后果，一个可预见的意外，

cues.en: look at Challenger.
cues.zh: 看看“挑战者号”。

cues.en: Challenger was no accident. Challenger was a predictable surprise. At the time that rocket came apart scattered throughout masseter contractors and filing cabinets and desk drawers were written documents, memos predicting that the exact thing that did happen,
cues.zh: “挑战者号”事故并非偶然。“挑战者号”事故是一个可预见的意外。当时，那枚火箭解体时，在各个承包商办公室、文件柜和办公桌抽屉里，都存放着书面文件和备忘录，预测了后来确实发生的事情，

cues.en: I. E. Failure of this o ring was going to happen. And where did people get the information to make such predictions? From the best source available, flight data. It doesn't get any better than to get the piece back and see how it performed.
cues.zh: 也就是 O 形圈会失效。那么，人们依据什么做出这样的预测？依据的是最可靠的信息来源：飞行数据。没有什么比把部件找回来、看看它实际表现如何更可靠了。

cues.en: And that's the case with these solid rocket boosters. They're not throwaway items. 25 miles up, they burn out, they're jettisoned, they have gigantic parachutes that are deployed. These things are lowered into the water. Air is trapped inside them when they hit, so they float. Tugboats are positioned out there to put a line on them, tow them back to shore. There they're cleaned up, taken apart, inspected, and used over again. The operative word in this process is inspected.
cues.zh: 固体火箭助推器就是这种情况。它们不是一次性用品。升到 25 英里高空后，燃料烧尽，助推器被抛弃，并展开巨大的降落伞。这些东西会降落到水中。撞击水面时，内部会困住空气，所以它们能漂浮起来。拖船会在海上待命，把缆绳系到助推器上，再拖回岸边。之后，它们会被清理、拆解、检查，然后再次使用。这个流程中的关键词就是“检查”。

cues.en: And on 14 of 24 flights before Challenger, Challenger was number 25.
cues.zh: 在挑战者号之前的24次飞行中，有14次飞行里，挑战者号被编号为25号。

cues.en: On 14 of 24 flights before Challenger in the inspection process, quality assurance and safety people noted that the o rings, which were never designed to be touched by fire, were being touched by fire. And they understood the ramifications of their findings. This design is flawed. It's going to fail. People are going to die.
cues.zh: 在挑战者号之前的24次飞行中，有14次飞行的检查过程中，质量保证和安全人员都注意到，原本从未设计为接触火焰的 O 形密封圈，正在接触火焰。他们也明白这些发现意味着什么。这个设计有缺陷。它迟早会失效。人们会因此丧命。

cues.en: And they basically put words that effect in these various memos.
cues.zh: 他们基本上在这些备忘录中写下了类似的话。

cues.en: I want to share with you excerpts of two of these memos, both of which were written by Thycol engineers, the contractor,
cues.zh: 我想和大家分享其中两份备忘录的摘录，这两份备忘录都是由承包商 Thycol 的工程师撰写的，

cues.en: to their customer NASA.
cues.zh: 发给他们的客户 NASA。

cues.en: The first memo was dated February '84. This is two years before Challenger.
cues.zh: 第一份备忘录的日期是 1984 年 2 月，也就是挑战者号事故前两年。

cues.en: And in part, the memo reads,
cues.zh: 备忘录中有一段这样写道：

cues.en: the recent experience of two burned o rings on STS 11, that's the eleventh shuttle mission, raises concerns with STS 13.
cues.zh: “STS 11，也就是第 11 次航天飞机任务中，两个烧损 O 形密封圈的近期经历，引发了人们对 STS 13 的担忧。”

cues.en: You know, when I read this, I wonder how come nobody was concerned about STS 12,
cues.zh: 你知道，读到这里时，我不禁想，怎么没人担心 STS 12 呢？

cues.en: my first mission. But apparently
cues.zh: 那是我的第一次任务。但显然，

cues.en: apparently, they weren't.
cues.zh: 显然，他们并没有担心。

cues.en: The o ring leak check procedure is also an urgent concern. Your support in this urgent matter is requested.
cues.zh: O 形密封圈泄漏检查流程也是一个紧迫问题。请提供支持，协助处理这一紧迫事项。

cues.en: Two years before Challenger,
cues.zh: 就在挑战者号事故前两年，

cues.en: the label urgent has been hung on this o ring design. It's not working.
cues.zh: “紧迫”这个标签已经被贴在这种 O 形密封圈设计上了。它根本不起作用。

cues.en: Here's a sense out of a Thycol memo dated July '85. This is six months before Challenger.
cues.zh: 下面是 Thycol 一份日期为 1985 年 7 月的备忘录中的一段内容。这距离挑战者号事故还有六个月。

cues.en: The memo was written by mister Roger Boujolet, a Thycol rocket engineer.
cues.zh: 这份备忘录由 Thycol 的火箭工程师 Roger Boujolet 先生撰写。

cues.en: In his memo, he wrote a very prophetic sentence. Here it is.
cues.zh: 他在备忘录里写了一句非常有预见性的话。原文是这样的。

cues.en: It is my honest and very real fear
cues.zh: 我真诚且非常真实的恐惧是

cues.en: that if we do not take immediate action to dedicate a team to solve the problem with the field joint, and that's the o ring, having the number one priority,
cues.zh: 如果我们不立即行动，专门派一个团队去解决现场接缝的问题，也就是O型圈，把它列为最高优先级，

cues.en: then we stand in jeopardy of losing a flight, a crew, and all the launch pad facilities.
cues.zh: 那么我们就有可能失去一次飞行、一组宇航员，以及所有发射台设施。

cues.en: Mister Bourgelet's prediction was only off seventy three seconds. He thought the rocket was gonna blow up on the launch pad, destroy the vehicle, kill the crew, and take out the launch pad facilities.
cues.zh: 布尔热莱先生的预测只差了七十三秒。他以为火箭会在发射台上爆炸，摧毁飞行器，杀死宇航员，并摧毁发射台设施。

cues.en: He missed it by seventy three seconds. Challenger was no accident.
cues.zh: 他只差七十三秒就猜中了。挑战者号并非意外。

cues.en: Challenger was a predictable surprise.
cues.zh: 挑战者号是一场可预见的意外。

cues.en: Now I know what everybody's thinking right now. Why didn't the team react to these warnings, ground the fleet and fix the problem? And the answer is to a significant degree, the team was laboring under a long term normalization of deviance. And let me explain. Approximately a decade before Challenger, a standard of performance was established for these o rings in our failure modes and effects analysis document.
cues.zh: 我知道大家现在在想什么。为什么团队没有对这些警告做出反应，停飞整个机队并解决问题？答案在很大程度上是，团队长期处于一种对偏差的常态化之中。让我解释一下。大约在挑战者号事故十年前，我们在失效模式与影响分析文档中为这些O型圈确立了性能标准。

cues.en: They were given a criticality one label, meaning if they ever fail, it's loss of the vehicle and death to the crew. So a standard of performance was established for these o rings. They can never show any hint of a failure mode. If they fail, it's death.
cues.zh: 它们被标为关键性一级，意思是如果它们失效，就是飞行器损毁和宇航员死亡。所以这些O型圈有了性能标准。它们绝不能表现出任何失效模式的迹象。一旦失效，就是死亡。

cues.en: And de facto, you have now established a standard of performance and how the team should react if they ever see a problem with the o rings. Criticality one deviance, only one thing you can do, ground the fleet.
cues.zh: 事实上，你们现在已经确立了一套性能标准，以及团队一旦发现O型环出现问题时应如何反应。一级严重偏差，你唯一能做的就是停飞整个机队。

cues.en: But that standard of performance was established as I said about a decade before Challenger
cues.zh: 但正如我所说，这套性能标准是在挑战者号事故大约十年前确立的

cues.en: in a no pressure situation.
cues.zh: 而且是在没有压力的情境下。

cues.en: Emphasis on those words. When the first o ring damage is seen, it's not a no pressure situation.
cues.zh: 请着重体会这几个字。当首次发现O型环损伤时，那可不是没有压力的情境。

cues.en: First o ring damage is seen when they bring the boost... When they get the boosters back from the second shuttle mission. Now here you have leadership, quality assurance, safety people staring at their worst nightmare, evidence of a major design flaw in this multibillion dollar program.
cues.zh: 首次发现O型环损伤，是在他们取回助推器的时候……是在第二次航天飞机任务取回助推器时。此时，领导层、质量保证人员、安全人员正盯着他们最可怕的噩梦——这个耗资数十亿美元的项目存在重大设计缺陷的证据。

cues.en: And they can see how the standard of performance isn't violated. This is a Criticality one deviance we're looking at, a burned o ring.
cues.zh: 他们能看到如何才能不违反性能标准。我们面对的是一个一级严重偏差，一个烧损的O型环。

cues.en: And at that point, the standard for the team was what? Ground the fleet.
cues.zh: 而在那一刻，团队的标准是什么？停飞整个机队。

cues.en: You cannot fly with a criticality one deviance.
cues.zh: 存在一级严重偏差，就不能飞行。

cues.en: But the team could not bring themselves to adhere to that standard of performance established so, you know, those many years earlier. Why? Because it's not a no pressure situation.
cues.zh: 但团队却无法让自己遵守那么多年前确立的那套性能标准。为什么？因为这不是没有压力的情境。

cues.en: These people are at tremendous pressure not just to see the fleet continue to fly, but to rapidly expand the shuttle flight rate. It's laughable now to hear folks, but you know where we were headed in the early eighties with the shuttle flight rate, 26 missions a year. A shuttle was going to be flying every two weeks. And in fact, the shuttle made no economic sense if it wasn't flying at that flight rate. NASA had promised Congress and the American public
cues.zh: 这些人承受着巨大的压力，不仅要让机队继续飞行，还要迅速扩大航天飞机的飞行频率。现在听来很可笑，但你知道八十年代初我们在航天飞机飞行频率上的目标吗——每年26次任务。航天飞机每两周就要飞一次。事实上，如果不按那个频率飞行，航天飞机在经济上毫无意义。NASA曾向国会和美国公众承诺

cues.en: that shuttle would dramatically reduce the cost of operating a space because it was gonna be so easy to turn between missions.
cues.zh: 航天飞机将大幅降低太空运营成本，因为它在任务之间的周转会非常容易。

cues.en: It would just take a couple weeks from landing to get it back on the launch pad with new boosters, new gas tank, new payload, and it's ready to go again. And that business model, 26 missions a year became our god. Nothing could get in the way of that schedule.
cues.zh: 从着陆到重新回到发射台，换上新的助推器、新的燃料箱、新的有效载荷，只需要几周，然后就能再次出发。而这个商业模式——一年 26 次任务——成了我们的神。任何东西都不能挡这个进度。

cues.en: So now they're facing... The team is facing a criticality one deviance. They have a standard of performance that they're supposed to adhere to, ground the fleet.
cues.zh: 所以现在他们面临……团队正面对一个一级关键偏差。他们有本应遵守的性能标准：停飞机队。

cues.en: But under this tremendous pressure,
cues.zh: 但在这种巨大压力下，

cues.en: they start rationalizing
cues.zh: 他们开始合理化解释，

cues.en: why they can continue to fly or how to take a shortcut to accept a lower standard of performance.
cues.zh: 为什么还能继续飞，或者怎样走捷径、接受更低的性能标准。

cues.en: What they do is they take a pristine o ring. They intentionally
cues.zh: 他们的做法是拿一个完好的 O 型圈。然后故意

cues.en: damage it to a degree greater than what they saw in the damaged recovered o ring. They put that intentionally damaged o ring in a laboratory pressure test article. They pressurized it to 3,000 psi,
cues.zh: 把它损坏到比回收到的受损 O 型圈更严重的程度。再把这个故意损坏的 O 型圈装进实验室压力测试件，加压到 3,000 psi，

cues.en: three times the pressure we'd ever see in flight, and that damaged o ring held pressure.
cues.zh: 也就是我们在飞行中会看到的压力的三倍，而这个受损 O 型圈承受住了压力。

cues.en: So the team rationalized, hey, even a damaged o ring is holding pressure. And in flight, the backup o ring held pressure, so we don't need to ground the fleet.
cues.zh: 于是团队就合理化了：嘿，连受损的 O 型圈都能保住压力。飞行中备份 O 型圈也保住了压力，所以我们不需要停飞机队。

cues.en: We can make some minor assembly processes and hope that fixes the problem, collect some data on the fly. We can continue flight operations
cues.zh: 我们可以改一些小的装配流程，希望这样能解决问题，并在飞行中边飞边收集数据。我们可以继续飞行，

cues.en: in spite of a criticality one deviance.
cues.zh: 尽管存在一个一级关键偏差。

cues.en: So they take the shortcut.
cues.zh: 于是他们走了捷径。

cues.en: And while I'm telling this story, I hope all of you were thinking about how many times you have rationalized.
cues.zh: 在我讲这个故事的时候，我希望你们都在想：自己有多少次也这样合理化过。

cues.en: We're all human. We all come under pressure. How many times have you rationalized it's okay to take the shortcut?
cues.zh: 我们都是人。我们都会承受压力。有多少次，你为自己找理由说走捷径也没关系？

cues.en: So now here the NASA team has rationalized it's okay to take the shortcut.
cues.zh: 所以现在，NASA团队也为自己找了理由：走捷径没关系。

cues.en: You know, they... What they've what they've done here now is accepted something that was never expected.
cues.zh: 你知道，他们……他们现在在这里所做的，就是接受了一件从未被预期的事情。

cues.en: Wasn't that the O rings were designed to take damage and continue to function. They were never to see damage.
cues.zh: O型环的设计不就是要承受损伤并继续工作吗？它们本来绝不该出现损伤。

cues.en: But in this pressure cooker, the team has rationalized
cues.zh: 但在这种高压锅般的环境里，团队已经合理化了

cues.en: why it's okay to see some damage, something that's not expected and not understood
cues.zh: 为什么看到一些损伤也没关系，即便那是未预期、也没被理解的东西

cues.en: and flight operations continue.
cues.zh: 并且飞行任务继续。

cues.en: And guess what the consequences are?
cues.zh: 猜猜后果是什么？

cues.en: There are no bad consequences.
cues.zh: 没有糟糕的后果。

cues.en: The next couple of missions return pristine o ring, boosters
cues.zh: 接下来几次任务返回的助推器，O型环都完好如初，

cues.en: that show pristine o rings.
cues.zh: 显示出完好的O型环。

cues.en: And every time they break apart one of those boosters, see those perfect o rings, what's that doing? Looping back into the brains of the NASA team, it was okay to take the shortcut in the first place.
cues.zh: 而每次他们拆开其中一个助推器，看到那些完美的O型环，这会产生什么作用？它反复回馈到NASA团队的脑中：一开始走捷径就是没问题的。

cues.en: Then they get the o ring... The boosters back from the sixth shuttle mission. They see more damaged o rings. What happens now? We're deeper into the program. The expectations are higher. The promises have been made are greater. Harder now to go back to that original standard of performance that says ground the fleet. And now they have that history of having gotten away within the past, it becomes a little bit easier to rationalize why it's okay to continue flight operations again. So they make some more minor assembly process changes and continue flight operations.
cues.zh: 然后他们拿回第六次航天飞机任务的O型环……拿回助推器。他们看到更多受损的O型环。现在会怎样？项目推进得越深，期望就越高，做出的承诺也越大。此时再回到最初那个要求停飞整个机队的性能标准，就更难了。而既然他们有过过去侥幸过关的历史，再找理由说为什么可以继续飞行任务，就变得稍微容易一些。于是他们又做了一些小的装配流程改动，并继续飞行任务。

cues.en: Basically, what's happening here folks is the damage seen on flight two is slowly becoming the umbrella.
cues.zh: 基本上，这里发生的情况是，二号航班上看到的损伤正慢慢变成常态。

cues.en: And the team slowly starts rationalizing. As long as we never see damage that exceeds what we saw on flight two, it's okay to continue flight operations.
cues.zh: 团队开始慢慢合理化。只要损伤不超过二号航班上看到的程度，就可以继续飞行。

cues.en: Well, for another dozen times or so, they get back boosters that... Where the damage to the o rings doesn't exceed what they saw in flight two until on flight 25, Challenger's mission, the damage exceeds in a great way what they saw in flight two.
cues.zh: 又飞了十几次，他们拿回来的助推器……O型环的损伤都没超过二号航班的程度，直到第25次任务，挑战者号，损伤大大超出了二号航班的水平。

cues.en: Total primary back... Total primary and backup o ring failure, loss of the vehicle in the death of seven astronauts.
cues.zh: 主O型环和备份O型环完全失效，飞行器损毁，七名宇航员遇难。

cues.en: Basically, by the time Challenger was occurring, a large body of the team that was working this o ring problem had come to expect to see o ring damage.
cues.zh: 基本上，到挑战者号出事时，团队里很大一部分处理O型环问题的人已经预期会看到O型环损伤了。

cues.en: Now I want you to think about that. We've gone from something we correctly defined as intolerable to accept to something over four years and 24 missions has become what?
cues.zh: 现在想想看。我们从一件被正确界定为不可容忍的事，经过四年多、24次任务，变成了什么？

cues.en: Expected.
cues.zh: 习以为常。

cues.en: Normalization of deviance. It is a killer of teams, folks, literally in hazardous environments. It will kill people.
cues.zh: 偏差的正常化。各位，这是团队的杀手，在危险环境中 literally 会要人命。它会害死人。
